chunks: Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in exchanging one camel for two camels, and one animal for two animals, hand to hand.
And he said: There is no harm in exchanging one garment for two garments, hand to hand or on deferred terms, if you describe them.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: a garment or piece of clothing as a trade item
key_terms.الدَّابَّةُ: a riding animal or beast exchanged in trade
key_terms.اَلْبَعِيرُ: a camel being exchanged as a sale item
key_terms.وَصَفْتَهُمَا: you describe both items so that their qualities are known
key_terms.يَدًا بِيَدٍ: an immediate hand-to-hand exchange without delay

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to exchange one camel for two camels or one garment for two garments in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on exchanging certain non-ribawi goods in unequal amounts. It permits trading one animal for two animals hand to hand, and one garment for two garments either immediately or on deferred terms, provided the items are described properly.
